refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: platformd-verifyd.service is a system service that verifies the presence of the calling user. On request it runs the platformd-verify PAM stack. On success it submits the result to platformd-trustd.service8 when that service is available. Completion of this best-effort submission does not affect the verification result. Requests may be made with verifyctl1.

The user verified is always the caller's own, taken from the peer credentials of the connection rather than from a claimed name. The target must be an active, local, logind-reported unlocked session owned by that user. An explicitly named session is never replaced by another session. If no session is named, the service uses the caller's eligible session. If the caller is not associated with a session, the service selects the only eligible session for the caller.
The service drives PAM and therefore runs privileged. It announces readiness through sd_notify3 and terminates cleanly on SIGTERM.

refsect1.title: The Varlink interface
refsect1.para: The service exposes a single varlink7 interface, io.platformd.Verify, on a AF_UNIX socket at /run/platformd-verifyd/io.platformd.Verify. The method VerifyUser, takes the session to refresh and a human-readable reason, runs the PAM stack, and returns whether the user was verified together with the PAM service that ran. The reason is descriptive text supplied by the client. It is not a verified application identity. Authentication responses do not cross this interface.

VerifyUserWithMessages has the same authentication semantics and requires the Varlink more flag. Intermediate replies contain a message with style (info or error) and text. The terminal reply contains only result, with the fields returned by VerifyUser, or an error. Only PAM informational and error messages are forwarded. No input prompts or authentication responses are forwarded, and no message response is accepted. Delivery is bounded to 32 messages of 1024 bytes each. Invalid records, overflow, or delivery failure cancel verification. Slow clients do not block the worker or the service. Messages contain PAM module text and do not establish a trusted UI. VerifyUser remains outcome-only. Message delivery is opt-in for each client; it does not add presentation to existing callers or unrelated desktop agents.

VerifyUserWithContext uses the same message and result contract and accepts an additional context object. Its challengeHex and operationDigestHex fields each encode exactly 32 bytes in hexadecimal. Its audience field contains 1 through 256 printable ASCII bytes. The context is copied before authentication; hexadecimal values are converted to lowercase. The audience is not normalized. The context is application-supplied data, not a verified origin or an authentication response. It must not contain secrets and is not passed to PAM.

After successful authentication and final session validation, SubmitVerificationEvent is attempted on io.platformd.Trust with the caller's user, UID, session, immutable context, and verificationBoottimeUSec and verificationRealtimeUSec sampled using CLOCK_BOOTTIME and CLOCK_REALTIME. These timestamps denote completion after worker cleanup and final session validation, not the instant the PAM module returned. Submission is asynchronous and bounded to two seconds. At most 64 authentication submissions may remain pending. Missing services, unsupported methods, full queues, and recording failures do not change the completed PAM result. A contextual request never submits an ordinary authentication event as a fallback.

The result does not establish measurement, remote acceptance, approval of the described operation, or success of a particular factor. No attestation token is returned through this interface. A remote verifier must require the exact context in complete, challenge-bound evidence, check its enrolled key and policy, and enforce challenge expiry and single use using its own clock. Device timestamps do not establish remote freshness. Ordinary verification and previously recorded freshness do not satisfy that check.

The PAM conversation runs in a supervised worker, so a factor that waits at the reader does not block the service. One verification runs for each user at a time, with a bounded number across the machine. A concurrent call for the same user is refused with Busy. The worker is terminated when its client disconnects, the target session becomes ineligible, or the service deadline expires. Remaining forked descendants are terminated and reaped before the request completes or its concurrency slot is released. This includes helpers that create separate process sessions.

The supervisor uses the procfs children interface to collect orphaned descendants. It does not run PAM and closes inherited descriptors other than standard input, output, and error. A dedicated nonblocking message descriptor is passed only to the PAM worker and closed on subsequent exec. The PAM worker re-executes the service binary before loading the stack, so libraries do not retain stale descriptor state from the daemon. Service-wide termination uses the systemd control group. Worker supervision is a lifetime boundary, not a sandbox for privileged PAM modules.

NoSession is returned if no logind session can be resolved. AmbiguousSession is returned if more than one eligible session remains. SessionNotEligible is returned if an explicitly named session is not eligible. PromptUnavailable reports that a compatible password agent could not accept a prompt. VerificationTimedOut and VerificationCancelled report deadline and cancellation failures.

refsect1.title: Factors
refsect1.para: The factors offered are the auth lines of the platformd-verify PAM stack (/usr/lib/pam.d/platformd-verify, overridable under /etc/pam.d/). The vendor stack uses pam_fprintd.so. Administrators may configure other PAM authentication modules. PAM control flags determine the final authentication result. A successful stack result is not overridden by an earlier password conversation failure. Message-delivery failure, request cancellation, and the service deadline remain independent of that result.

PAM password and PIN prompts are sent to the per-user io.systemd.AskPassword Varlink service. Prompt caching is disabled. A compatible systemd password presenter must be available for an interactive prompt to succeed. The interface addresses a user, not an individual session; session eligibility does not bind prompt presentation to that session. A polkit agent does not implement this interface. The prompt identifies platformd-verifyd and labels the client-supplied request description. It does not assert an application identity or a trusted graphical origin. Replies are returned only to PAM. The Varlink input is marked sensitive before reception, and response copies owned by verifyd are erased before release. PAM owns the responses delivered to its modules. Informational and error messages are written to the journal without authentication responses.

The verification deadline uses CLOCK_BOOTTIME and is checked again before a successful result is returned. logind queries are asynchronous and bounded to two seconds. Loss of the system bus stops the service; the unit restarts it after five seconds.
The reported method names the PAM service, not the individual PAM module that accepted the authentication.
